name: market-parity
note: A COMPOSITE IDENTITY, driven where a single-path reading gives a different answer. Stall 1 exists in row A and in row B and they are not the same pitch, so a runtime keying on the number alone finds A/1 when told B/1, and one keying on the row alone lets the whole row at once. Every step below distinguishes those two mistakes from the right answer: the pair is opened, both are let separately, one is vacated and re-let while the other stays let, and the refusals name the identity as the bluebook declared it — both paths, in order.

steps.note: THE DISCRIMINATING PAIR — same number, different row. A runtime that joins only the first path has already overwritten A/1 here.
B/1 is still vacant. Keyed on the number alone this is refused as already let.
A/2 is still vacant. Keyed on the row alone this is refused as already let.
REFUSED — A/1 really is let, and the given says so.
A/1 is vacant again and takes a new trader; B/1 must be untouched by all of it.
REFUSED — B/1 was never vacated, so this must find B/1 let and not A/1 vacant.
REFUSED — HALF an identity names nothing. A row with no number must not fall back to the first path and let A/1.
REFUSED — a creating command that cannot say which one this is gets no minted identity, and the refusal quotes both declared paths.
REFUSED by the invariant, not by the identity — a stall is numbered from one.
A COMPOSITE PIECE UNDER A COMPOSITE HEAD. The parent is joined from row+number before the element is matched on day+session.
SAME DAY, other session — the pair that tells a first-part match from a whole-identity one.
SAME SESSION, other day — the mirror of the pair above, so neither part alone can be standing in for the identity.
A booking on the OTHER stall of the same number, so the piece lookup cannot key on the day alone across parents either.
Confirms MONDAY AFTERNOON on A/1. Matching on the day alone confirms the morning instead; matching on the session alone confirms Tuesday.
REFUSED — monday morning on A/1 is still held, so this must succeed... and it does. The one after it is the refusal.
REFUSED — monday afternoon on A/1 is already confirmed. A first-part match would find the morning here and refuse for the wrong reason.
REFUSED — no such slot. Wednesday was never booked on A/1, and neither part of the identity may stand in for the whole.
REFUSED — HALF a piece identity names nothing, the same as half a head's. A day with no session must not fall through to the first slot of that day.
REFUSED by the session invariant — morning or afternoon, and "evening" is neither.
